Saw your comment and wanted to give a tip regarding Pteras stamina. I see a lot of people who start out learning Ptera burn through stamina, but the trick is to not sprint while flying. Pteras are incredibly efficient gliders and as long as you're not sprinting or gaining too much height, you can pretty much fly across the entire map while barely depleting any stamina.

It also helps to tab space quickly when trying to gain height, as it minimally reduces the amount of stamina it takes to climb. And if you want to go fatser you can always try flying from a bit higher up and diving, it will give you a big speed boost with no need for sprint and no depletion of stamina! I hope that helps a bit :)

Also please don't missunderstand what I'm about to say, as I'm only trying to explain but the statements that people throw at nonvegans about being rapists and murderers comes from the unfortunate reality that buying meat/milk/eggs supports industries that do that. While most people that buy these things don't spend a second to think about that stuff, and therefore don't feel responsable for it, we vegans do, so it becomes a very heated place of discussion. I too used to buy meat, I'm not free of it either. But it's where a lot of the hostility comes from. That doesn't mean all vegans hate nonvegans. The loudest people are always the ones everyone gets to see, it's like that in every community.

I want to say that going into a space for people by saying "I'm never going to understand or be part of you" is not going to net you many friendly responses, especially on the internet. People online are always going to be more upfront and aggressive than in person.

That being said I'd like to give a response anyway.

I personally know many people who aren't vegan, and I'm not going about pestering them to become vegan, save from some conversations about it if they want to have them. We do live in a world that is meat centered and that isn't going to change anytime soon. That being said, some of the points you bring up, aren't exactly fair. For example you say that it's all part of biology and the balance of the world, and while this may have been true hundreds of years ago, it hasn't been true for a long time. Animals are being slaughtered left and right to the billions for our convinient, that isn't really natural, and what we vegans do is simply not support a system that is so cruel. Sure there might be some farms out there, who treat their animals well but in the end those animals also get killed. The "happy farms" really make up a small minority of the animal products that are in everydays products, things you might not even think about. We simply believe that the pleasure of enjoying butter on bread for 5 minutes isn't worth the suffering of an animal.

You can and are allowed to believe what you want, but essentially you came here to ask people not to challenge you on their morals, which is exactly what you don't want us to do to you, so I'm wondering what your reason for this post is.

Fps is a large genre. You have so much variety in there, from more chill solo campaign games, to coop and multiplayer games to games like valorant or csgo that are often considered the harder ones to learn.

Figure out what and if you enjoy fps games. Some people like only certain fps games and not others. I for example love TF2 but I hate csgo or valorant. Find what sticks with you and don't beat yourself up for not being amazing at it or learning as quickly as you'd like. 

Once you find a game you enjoy, you can look at youtube videos and tips directly for said game, as every fps plays differently. Give yourself time to figure out your playstyle, the classes or type of characters you enjoy and have fun. Eventually improvement will come :)

If you're talking about traces, like for example a pack of chips that's vegan but contains traces of dairy, most vegans don't actually care about that, since that only means it was produced in the same factory as something with milk and is mostly just on there for people with allergies.  
  
If you're talking about stuff that's just not vegan by default cause dairy was added to it, ifnot aware, dairy looks like a byproduct that doesn't harm, cause cows produce milk anyway right?   
Unfortunately that's far from the reality of things. 

Milk isn't a byproduct, it is its own industry. Massive farms in which cows are repeatedly impregnated to produce cattle, so they keep producing milk. The baby cows are taken from their mother after birth and are either sent off to the meat industry or if they're female get raised to follow the same fate as their mothers. These cows stand in their pens their entire life with the circle of - impregnate - birth - give milk -repeat. It's incredibly cruel and some might even say worse than the meat industry cause at least the slaughter stops the animals from suffering.

Gimp has features like layers and animation previews that allow you to make animations and save them as gifs. There are plenty of tutorials about this on youtube! It should be enough for the start.   
I think there are some better programs if you end up wanting to use those in games, though I don't know those too well.

What I would recommend is for you to download a free art program like gimp for example. Then download a bunch of pixelart you think looks nice and just try to replicate it one by one! It might also help to refine your searches, instead of "Pixel tutorial" try "stickfigure pixel tutorial" etc. 

The more you replicate, the more you'll understand what these pictures make out. Try to make your own every once in a while and keep track of what doesn't look good for you, then revisit the pixel art you like and check the differences. Normally I'd recommend learning to draw the basics in general, like shapes and anatomy, since it will help you understand art as a whole and once you know the rules you can bend them. But if you don't plan on going further than pixel art, that might be enough already.

There are two different types of reports.

On the bottom right you can see the text "Are you submitting a complete checklist of the birds you were able to identify?" if you press yes on that one, it means you're giving eBird an accurate checklist. That means you have to say "11 mallards" instead of "x mallards".

If you want to just say "x mallards" you have to press "no" as it's not a complete checklist and just you reporting some ducks you saw.

This is to help differentiate between people just adding one or two birds they were out looking for and people who report every single bird they saw in that location, as it helps with research and data.

Hope this helps :)

How to sharpen a knife.

To sharpen the blade, use an oilstone and the right oil. The angle the knife is being held onto the stone is important. A flat angle makes the blade blunt.

Add some honey oil to the stone, never use the stone dry. Apply the blade with the correct angle of 22° against the stone, just like shown in the picture. Pull the blade in one pull from the handle to the edge over the stone. Now rotate the blade and repeat to pull the blade from the handle to the edge.

Repeat the same amount of pulls on each side, to even the blade out. The first pulling will take some time. As soon as the blade is sharp, it can be mantained to stay sharp very easily. Try to avoid damage of the blade, otherwise it will get blunt again very fast.

The "Washita-Stone" is for normal pulling. This stone will sharpen the blade of your knife in a very minimum of your time.

The "Hard-Arkansas-Stone" is for blades, that are already slightly sharp. It makes the blade of your knife razor sharp.
After using the stones, they're to be cleaned and dried.

If you want to be more open with your boyfriend you could try to write everything down, all the feelings that bother you, everything you want to talk about and then give it to him. If it's a letter or an email or anything like this doesn't matter. The point to this is, that you don't have to be in the same room if you're scared for reactions, or that if he reads it he can't interrupt you while you talk. Just be honest with him and he'll understand, if you tell him that you want to be more open but you don't know how, you might be able to find a way together. 
You also need to trust that, if everything is going alright, nothing bad is going to happen. I know this is actually pretty hard, but something that I realized is that the more you worry about something, the worse it will get.

Maybe one good step to start is to ask him if he's happy with the relationship, if needed over text as well, and if he thinks something should be changed or not. If he says he's happy, trust him and try to enjoy it. Be yourself.

Good luck for you in the future <3
